subject: science
passage: Hummingbirds burn energy very quickly, and during the day they must feed every few minutes. At night, when they cannot feed, many hummingbirds enter a state called torpor. Their body temperature drops, and their heart rate slows sharply. This deep rest greatly reduces the amount of energy they use, helping them survive until morning, when they can feed again.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Hummingbirds must feed every few minutes during the day.
choices.B: Hummingbirds sleep for more hours each night than other birds.
choices.C: Many hummingbirds survive the night by slowing their bodies to save energy.
choices.D: Hummingbirds' heart rates rise sharply when they rest at night.

explanation.why: The text sets up a problem (hummingbirds use energy fast but cannot feed at night) and then explains the solution: torpor, in which body temperature and heart rate drop, which "greatly reduces the amount of energy they use." The main idea is how torpor helps them survive the night.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Feeding every few minutes is a detail from the first sentence that sets up the main point.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never compares hummingbirds' sleep with that of other birds.
explanation.C: Correct. This covers the problem and the solution: during torpor their bodies slow down, saving energy until morning.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says their heart rate "slows sharply," not that it rises.
